questions.question: Which activity is explicitly described as part of the requirements elicitation process?

options.B: Prioritizing requirements after they are documented
options.C: Discovering and understanding stakeholder needs such as application domain and performance expectations

questions.explanation:
The context states that during requirements elicitation software engineers work with stakeholders to learn about the application domain, work activities, services, performance, and hardware constraints [Page 12].

---

questions.question: What is the main purpose of requirements validation as outlined in the context?

options.A: To assess the technical feasibility of the system
options.B: To ensure that the documented requirements truly reflect the real needs of system users
options.D: To negotiate the order of implementation for each requirement

questions.explanation:
Requirements validation is defined as the process of checking that requirements define the system the customer really wants, focusing on whether they reflect real user needs [Page 29].

---

questions.question: Which piece of stakeholder information is NOT mentioned as something engineers should discover during elicitation?

options.A: The required performance of the system
options.B: The hardware constraints affecting the system
options.C: The marketing budget for the product
options.D: The work activities performed by users

questions.explanation:
The text lists application domain, work activities, services, performance, and hardware constraints, but does not mention marketing budget as part of elicitation [Page 12].

---

questions.question: According to the described elicitation and analysis process, what follows the “Requirements discovery and understanding” step?
questions.explanation:
The process flow shows “Requirements discovery and understanding” followed by “Requirements documentation, classification and organization” [Page 13].

---

questions.question: Which of the following is a guideline for conducting effective requirements elicitation?

options.A: Concentrate only on functional requirements and ignore non‑functional concerns
options.B: Assume stakeholder needs remain unchanged throughout the project
options.C: Actively engage stakeholders to understand their work activities and domain context
options.D: Defer stakeholder involvement until after a complete design is drafted

questions.explanation:
The context emphasizes working with stakeholders to learn about the application domain, work activities, and other needs during elicitation [Page 12].

---

questions.question: In the spiral view of the requirements engineering process, which activity directly follows requirements elicitation?

options.C: Performing user validation of the requirements

questions.explanation:
The spiral view lists “User validation” as a phase that occurs after requirements elicitation and prototyping steps [Page 12].

---

questions.question: Which characteristic is highlighted as essential for a good requirements specification?

options.A: Ambiguity, to allow flexibility in design
options.C: Consistency, ensuring no conflicting statements exist
options.D: Difficulty of understanding, to protect intellectual property

questions.explanation:
A good requirements specification should be clear, unambiguous, complete, and consistent; consistency is specifically mentioned as a desired trait [Page 20].

---

questions.question: Which activity overlaps with requirements elicitation according to the context?
questions.explanation:
The text notes that requirements validation overlaps with elicitation and analysis because it looks for problems in the requirements [Page 29].

---

questions.question: During validity checks in the validation phase, what specific aspect of a requirement is examined?

options.A: Whether the requirement aligns with the project budget
options.B: Whether the requirement reflects the real needs of system users
options.C: Whether the requirement follows coding standards
options.D: Whether the requirement specifies performance metrics

questions.explanation:
Validity checks are described as ensuring that requirements reflect the real needs of users, especially when circumstances may have changed [Page 29].

---

questions.question: What best summarizes the overall goal of requirements elicitation as presented in the material?

options.A: To produce a working prototype as quickly as possible
options.B: To identify and thoroughly understand stakeholder needs and system constraints
options.C: To test the final system against performance criteria
options.D: To manage the project schedule and allocate resources

questions.explanation: The purpose of elicitation is to work with stakeholders to uncover domain knowledge, work activities, desired services, performance, and constraints, i.e., to understand stakeholder needs [Page 12].
